name: Agent Goal Hijack
existing_work: Reuses the ASI02 arena; Aegis Vector (injection and spotlighting results) is sibling evidence
limits_and_what_it_would_take: Agent stack: only a single retrieval-and-answer loop has been tested, not a tool-using planner. Needs: a tool-using agent crew in Greenroom, an adaptive red team that is not the author, and models above the 8B size this hardware allows.

name: Tool Misuse and Exploitation
existing_work: RealEstateTools MCP server (copied in) and a new Deal Desk server; first preregistered live run
limits_and_what_it_would_take: Two small MCP servers show the pattern, not the coverage. Needs a larger real tool catalog with realistic argument variety, an enterprise policy engine, a multi-step agent, and an attacker who is not the author.

name: Identity and Privilege Abuse
existing_work: First preregistered live run in this repository (simulated desk)
limits_and_what_it_would_take: Simulated desk, author-written attacks and gate, one agent step, three models up to 8B. Untested: credential lifetimes, mid-task revocation, the delegation-chain check, an escalation path. Needs a real identity provider (for example Entra ID or Okta) and workload identity, a multi-step agent, and an attacker who is not the author. A local simulation shows the logic, not production behavior.

name: Agentic Supply Chain Vulnerabilities
existing_work: The ASI02 calculator server with tampered stand-ins (a proxy)
limits_and_what_it_would_take: Needs an organizational registry, software bill of materials tooling, and real package ecosystems. A toy registry cannot show scale or incentive effects.

name: Unexpected Code Execution
limits_and_what_it_would_take: Needs production isolation (a micro-VM or user-space kernel) and a security review of the sandbox itself. A container on a workstation is a demonstration, not a boundary to trust.

name: Memory and Context Poisoning
owasp_llm_2025: LLM04 Data and Model Poisoning; LLM08 Vector and Embedding Weaknesses
limits_and_what_it_would_take: Registered facts only; an unregistered fact is admitted. Untested: the memory write path, slow drift, many agreeing forgeries, a poisoned verified corpus. Needs: larger models, an adaptive attacker who knows the gate, and a production-size corpus.

name: Insecure Inter-Agent Communication
limits_and_what_it_would_take: Needs agents on separate hosts or runtimes and a real key management service. A single-process crew cannot show network-level attacks.

name: Cascading Failures
existing_work: A three-agent crew on the ASI02 arena
limits_and_what_it_would_take: Needs production-scale topologies with many agents and real dependencies. A five-agent crew shows the mechanism, not the amplification factor.

name: Human-Agent Trust Exploitation
existing_work: AI reviewers measured in the ASI03 calibration run; a people study is built and waiting for participants
limits_and_what_it_would_take: Needs a human-subject study with real reviewers. Simulated reviewers cannot show how people actually fail.

name: Rogue Agents
limits_and_what_it_would_take: Needs long-horizon runs and real deployments to see slow drift. Short simulations underrepresent it.
